subject: Throughput profile & multiplexing constraints — post-call clarifications
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@beaconlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput profile & multiplexing constraints — post-call clarifications

Tara / Beacon team — thanks again for the demo call earlier. Quick post-call recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size capacity and propose a pilot config: 

Key takeaways (as I captured them)
- Primary flow: document ingestion -> chunking -> user query -> streaming + non-streaming responses to web/mobile clients.
- Expected average request size: ~1.2k tokens (after chunking; includes system + user).
- Mix: ~80% non-streaming single-shot responses, ~20% streaming chat-style responses.
- Current concurrency target: 12 steady-state concurrent in-flight requests, with short bursts up to ~130 QPS for ~60s during business events.
- Latency target: 95th <= 400ms single-shot; streaming initial token latency target ~350-500ms depending on client networks.
- Budget: looking for a predictable sizing + pilot for 6 weeks before committing to Dedicated.

Open clarifying questions for sizing (can you confirm the numbers below?):
1) Tokens per request: you mentioned ~1k on the call but slide shows 1.2k average; can you confirm the median and 95th token sizes?
2) Burst shape: is the ~130 QPS sustained for a full minute (steady high window) or a spiky 10-20s peak repeated during the hour? This affects batching and pre-warm needs.
3) Streaming concurrency: when a streaming session is active, do you keep the connection open until the user completes the session (avg session length)? Any client-side keep-alive/reconnect behavior we should anticipate?
4) Retry behavior: how often do clients retry on 500s/network glitches? Are retries exponential backoff or immediate?

Next steps I propose:
- You send a quick reply with the clarifications above (tokens median/95th, burst shape, streaming session length, retry patterns).
- I’ll produce two candidate pilot configs: a conservative config optimized for latency (smaller batch windows, reserved concurrency) and a cost-optimized config (aggressive batching + KV prefix caching) — deliver by EOD Friday.
- Schedule a 30-min engineering sync next week to walk the pilot plan and test harness (I’ll include Marissa for telemetry and Karthik for quant/profile tuning).

Attachments: I attached a very short load-sketch template (beacon-load-sketch.csv) — filling that helps us convert your numbers into a capacity sketch quickly.

Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Date: 2026-11-13T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profile & multiplexing constraints — post-call clarifications

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers and adding a few specifics from our side: 

- Tokens per request: median ~1,050; 95th ~2,400 (we see a tail for large manifests). The 1.2k I mentioned was a rough avg across logs.
- Burst shape: our peak traffic comes in short spikes tied to batch customer notifications. Typical pattern: 3-5 spikes per hour, each spike ~15-35s where QPS ramps to ~120-140, then drops back to baseline. So short, sharp spikes rather than minute-long sustained peaks.
- Steady-state QPS: baseline ~10-14 QPS (aligned with the 12 steady number).
- Streaming: average streaming session length ~22s (median 18s), active token churn during session ~150 tokens/sec on average. We typically keep connections open for the full session; clients do not aggressively reconnect.
- Retries: simple immediate retry once after a failure, then stop (no exponential backoff). We instrument retries at client side and can send a sample back.

I’m attaching a completed load sketch (.csv) with 24-hr sample projections and a short note on retry handling. Also adding our ops alias for any infra clarifications.

Tara Nguyen
VP, Product & Operations | Beacon Logistics
tara@beaconlogistics.com
Attachments: beacon-load-sketch.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara@beaconlogistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput profile & multiplexing constraints — post-call clarifications

Tara — perfect, this is very helpful. A few notes based on your numbers and the quick internal pass: 

Observations
- Short spike profile (15-35s) favors a pre-warm + rapid autoscale policy rather than very large reserved pools; we can reasonably size for steady-state and rely on burst buffer capacity for short spikes.
- The streaming token churn (150 tps during session) + 20% stream mix means concurrent token production can be high even if QPS is moderate — we’ll model token/sec as the primary billing and capacity axis.
- The 95th token tail to 2.4k means we should plan some headroom for KV cache miss scenarios; caching chunk embeddings can trim this but we should assume conservative perf until we validate.

Proposed pilot configs (high level) — I’ll put detailed numbers in the PDF attachment: 
1) Latency-first pilot: target 95p <= 400ms for single-shot and initial token <= 350ms for streaming. Config: reserved concurrency 16, small batch window (20ms), higher memory kv cache, conservative quant. Expected cost: higher, but predictable p95.
2) Cost-optimized pilot: target median latency within SLAs, allow p95 to float to 500ms under extreme spikes. Config: dynamic batching (50-120ms windows), aggressive KV caching + prefix caching enabled, larger multiplexing. Expected cost: ~30% lower in steady-state but higher tail latency risk.

Action items
- Ben: deliver PDFs with concrete GPU counts, estimated tokens/sec capacity, and cost delta by EOD Friday (I’ll attach redwood-sizing-notes.pdf).
- Marissa: propose telemetry hooks we’ll need from Beacon (trace/span names, token-length tagging) — can you propose a checklist by Friday?
- Karthik: run quick internal quant/cold-start sims against 1.2k median / 2.4k tail and share any immediate red flags by Thursday.

Schedule: suggest Tue 11/17 10:00am PT for the engineering sync; I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Ben
